A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SR-Reward work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reorganization: v1 includes Appendices A–D, and v2 includes Appendices A–H.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on MuJoCo, Adroit, Maniskill2, and a toy maze, including Table 1, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results and ablations, plus policy-action comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and online reinforcement-learning experiments.

M1.justification: The architecture, Algorithm 1, L2-norm reward, four training losses, negative-sampling rule, and 10,000-step warm start are retained. Renaming FC to MLP and testing the offline-trained reward with online RL do not establish a change to SR-Reward itself.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds a focused HalfCheetah scenario involving online interaction and exploration with an offline-trained reward. The existing toy-maze, MuJoCo, Adroit, and Maniskill2 task coverage is retained; Maniskill2 experiments already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: The new online experiment introduces true-reward TD3 as a comparator against TD3 using SR-Reward. BC, true-reward f-DVL and SparseQL, and VINS-style negative sampling remain in the corresponding retained comparisons.

E3.justification: Checkpoint evaluation changes from 10 to 25 rollouts, and final evaluation changes from 100 to 50 rollouts per seed. Maniskill training is reported as two million rather than one million steps. The data-size ablation drops the 1,000- and 5,000-trajectory conditions, while new analyses introduce action-comparison, hyperparameter-grid, and online-training protocols.

E4.justification: New Appendices F–H test policy-action agreement, sensitivity to negative-sampling hyperparameters, observation/action variability, and online applicability. V1's dataset-return variability study, including its small toy-maze comparison, is removed. Existing negative-sampling and data-quality ablations remain; the relocated data-size ablation uses fewer conditions.

E5.justification: The reported seed count increases explicitly from three to five. Table 1 changes from aggregating episode returns across seeds to reporting the mean and standard deviation of five per-seed mean returns. V1's Welch's t-test at significance level 0.05 and associated significance reporting are removed.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces many results under revised settings: SparseQL+SR-Reward on Walker2d changes from 85.57 ± 32.09 to 74.48 ± 7.85. It adds f-DVL+SR-Reward Maniskill results of 88.81, 70.71, and 35.44. New appendix findings cover action similarity, sensitivity, and weaker online performance; old return-variability results disappear. These are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V2 restores the missing discount factor gamma in the successor-feature recursion in Equation 1. Gamma was already present in v1's training loss and pseudocode, so this corrects the mathematical statement without establishing a method change. The occupancy-measure derivation is retained, moving from Appendix A to C.

C1.justification: The substantive contributions remain a policy-decoupled SR reward learned offline, concurrent integration with RL, and conservative negative sampling with competitive empirical performance. Calling it a reward module and mentioning Maniskill in the abstract clarify claims and coverage already present in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of action-policy similarity and hyperparameter failures, and explicitly questions the theoretical justification of the L2 reward conversion. It qualifies algorithm compatibility by noting that only two offline algorithms were tested. The dataset-variability explanation is removed, while the central limitation concerning extrapolation beyond demonstrations remains.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds practical guidance for selecting beta from observation/action variability and choosing sigma relative to beta. The retained corruption plot is newly identified as using Relocate, and normalization instructions explicitly include TurnFaucet. Conversely, v1's explicit no-gradient note for Bellman-target computation is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused comparison with preference-based reward learning, citing Christiano, Rafailov, Ethayarajh, and Bradley–Terry, plus supporting offline-RL, reward-clipping, and teleoperation references. Fujimoto and Gu (2021) and Hepburn and Montana (2023) are removed. The principal positioning relative to SR and IRL remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Background subsections are reordered, related work moves after experiments, and evaluation is organized around three explicit questions. Data-size and data-quality discussions move into appendices, and the broader-impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adds a training-pipeline diagram and four appendix figures, redraws the architecture diagram, and removes the old return-distribution figures and toy-maze statistics table. Ablation figures are relocated and revised, including fewer data-size categories. Table 1 loses significance shading, and captions and figure placement change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 makes variation between training runs clearer through five-seed summaries and adds useful sensitivity and online-failure tests. The corrected Equation 1 and clearer organization also help. These gains are moderated by removal of the return-variability analysis and an unexplained StackCube discrepancy: Figure 11 reports 83.51 at the stated main configuration, whereas Table 1 reports 71.03. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
